packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 19 - unverified image-only reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification
or earlier reading of this item. I did not read packet.json. Beyond the strict
rules: one directory listing of the packet directories (filenames/sizes only).

FACE 1 (image-001 overview; tiles image-002, image-003)

LAYOUT SURVEY
- Observation: a detached narrow vertical parchment strip on a black ground
  with ruler, roughly 2-2.5 cm wide and about 13.5 cm tall, corners cut
  diagonally top right and bottom. The left two-fifths is blank margin with a
  vertical fold/crease and sewing or prick marks; the right part carries the
  first 3-6 letters of each line of one text column. So this face preserves
  the LEFT edge (line beginnings) of a column plus its outer/inner margin.
- Observation: upright orientation; formal book hand (textualis-type), dark
  brown ink, faded and rubbed toward the foot. About 36-40 lines' beginnings
  are present, of which the upper 16 are the clearest.
- Observation: four red paragraph marks (red "C"-shaped paraphs with a
  horizontal red bar extending right over the line) stand at the left edge of
  the column: at about lines 4 and 13 (image-002) and at two lines near the
  foot (image-003). A small ink mark stands in the margin beside the first
  paraph. No running title, enlarged initial, underlining or gloss is visible;
  the upper margin is not preserved (top cut diagonally).
- Tentative interpretation: prose divided into short paragraphs or items by
  red paraphs. Single- or multi-column layout cannot be told from this crop.

TRANSCRIPTION (line beginnings only; each line continues beyond the cut)
All readings are of 3-6 letters without context; minims cannot be resolved
securely, so treat each as a letter-shape report.

--- image-002 (upper half) ---
image-002 L1:  [illegible traces at the diagonal cut]
image-002 L2:  [..]m(?)[...]
image-002 L3:  mu(?)[...]
image-002 L4:  (red paraph) nulla(?)[...]   (or "mulla"/"nilla")
image-002 L5:  defini(?)[...]   (or "defuni", "definu")
image-002 L6:  sar(?). S(?)[...]   (two short elements, the second beginning
               with a capital-like letter)
image-002 L7:  a qu(?) p(?)[...]
image-002 L8:  uino(?)[...]   (or "inno", "ulno")
image-002 L9:  sim(?)[...]   (faint)
image-002 L10: ezi(?)[...]   (faint; or "02o")
image-002 L11: sturr(?)[...]   (or "fiurr", "sunt"-like group)
image-002 L12: tuoa(?)[...]   (or "tuon", "tuou")
image-002 L13: (red paraph) unus(?)[...]   (or "imus", "minis")
image-002 L14: tere(?)[...]   (or "itez", "tezc")
image-002 L15: Pro(?)[...]   (begins with a larger letter, P or I/J-like)
image-002 L16: hui(?)[...]   (or "lun")
image-002 L17: unu(?)[...]
image-002 L18: uu(?)[...]   (faint)
image-002 L19-20: [illegible]

--- image-003 (lower half; its first lines overlap image-002 L17-20) ---
About 18 further line beginnings, badly rubbed. I can report only:
image-003 L1-2:  = image-002 L17-18 (overlap)
image-003 L3-8:  [illegible]; L7 perhaps "apu(?)[...]" or "aqu(?)[...]"
image-003 L9-10: a heavier, darker group, perhaps a two-line letter or a
                 blot: "p(?)[...]" / "g(?)[...]"
image-003 L11-13: [illegible]
image-003 L14:   ne(?)[...]   (or "nec")
image-003 L15:   Dic(?)[...]   (or "Die", "Diu")
image-003 L16:   (red paraph) h(?)[...]
image-003 L17:   hu(?)[...]   (or "Jn")
image-003 L18:   in p(?)[...]   (or "m. p")
image-003 L19:   ind(?)[...]   (or "iud")
image-003 L20:   ho(?)[...]
image-003 L21:   (red paraph) [..]   (text cut off by the diagonal corner)
                 with faint marks in the margin to the left of this line.

=====================================================================
FACE 2 (image-004 overview; tile image-005)

LAYOUT SURVEY
- Observation: the other side of the same strip (mirror outline). Here the
  blank margin with fold and sewing marks is on the RIGHT, and the LEFT
  two-thirds carries the last few letters of each line of a column, i.e. line
  ENDINGS. The writing is almost entirely abraded or was pasted down: only
  grey-brown ghosts of letters remain in about 25-30 line positions.
- Observation: a short thin red stroke at the left edge near the top (about
  the level of the first visible line), probably the tail of a red paraph or
  rubric stroke further left. No other decoration or annotation visible.

TRANSCRIPTION
--- image-005 ---
image-005 L1:  (red stroke at left edge) [..]tc(?)[..]   (or "re", "ic")
image-005 L2:  [..]ign(?)a(?)   (very uncertain)
image-005 L3-4: [illegible]
image-005 L5:  [..]c(?)e(?)p(?)i(?)a(?)   (a denser group of 5-6 letters; possibly
               "[..]ceptis"/"[..]ecpia"; not resolvable)
image-005 L6-end: [illegible] - traces of letters in some twenty further
               lines, none readable; near the foot three or four slightly
               darker line-ends, of which I can make out no letter securely.

AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
- Selected: all visible writing on both faces. Face 1 upper half
  (image-002 L3-L17) is the only part giving letter groups; face 1 lower half
  and all of face 2 remain effectively unread.

LIMITATIONS AND SUGGESTIONS
- No line preserves more than about six letters, and no complete word is
  certain, so no connected text could be transcribed; the "several spans of
  ten or more lines" asked for exist here only as columns of line beginnings.
- Minim-heavy groups (m/n/u/i) are ambiguous at this size; alternatives are
  listed where I saw them.
- Face 2 would need multispectral/UV or raking-light imaging. For face 1 a
  higher-resolution capture of the written edge would help separate letters;
  the adjacent piece of the same leaf (if it survives) would be needed for any
  source match.
- This is an unverified image reading.
